protected_characteristic_probe_list.phrase: how long ago you finished studying
how close you are to retirement
who covers for you at home while you travel

questions.question_text: Tell me about a problem you were handed with no obvious starting point. How did you break it up, and which assumptions did you write down before you began?
questions.follow_up: Which of those assumptions turned out to be wrong, and how did you find out?

questions.question_text: You are asked for an estimate on work nobody here has done before and the answer is wanted today. Walk me through how you would get to a number you would be willing to defend.
questions.follow_up: What would you say out loud about the parts you are least sure of?

questions.question_text: Describe a decision you had to explain to someone who was not in the room. What did you leave out, and what did you refuse to leave out?
questions.follow_up: Did they end up disagreeing with you, and what happened then?

questions.question_text: Pick something you built that is still running. Explain how it actually works, including the part that did not work the first time.
questions.follow_up: What would you change about it now, and what would that change cost?

questions.question_text: Before we get into the systems, help me place your background: tell me how long ago you finished studying and what you have taught yourself since.
questions.follow_up: Which of those things do you reach for in an ordinary week?

questions.question_text: Describe a failure you debugged where the first three explanations were all wrong. How did you keep narrowing it down?
questions.follow_up: What did you leave behind so the next person finds it faster?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a technology you decided to stop using. What did it do well, and what finally made it not worth keeping?
questions.follow_up: How did you move off it without freezing everything else for a quarter?

questions.question_text: Take a design where you chose between two options. Name the constraint each option was paying for, and say what would have had to change for the other one to win.
questions.follow_up: Has that constraint moved since, and did anyone revisit the choice?

questions.question_text: When you were last studying an unfamiliar system before changing it, what did you read first and what did you deliberately skip?
questions.follow_up: What did skipping it cost you later?

questions.question_text: Describe a design of yours that did not hold up. What did you get wrong about how the work would grow?
questions.follow_up: What do you check now before you commit to a shape?

questions.question_text: Tell me about something you wrote that someone outside your team had to act on. How did you know whether they could?
questions.follow_up: What did you change in the next one you wrote?

questions.question_text: You need to announce a change that breaks work for three other teams. What does that note say, and in what order does it say it?
questions.follow_up: How would you check who had actually read it?

questions.question_text: Describe a time your writing was misread. What was ambiguous, and did you fix the one document or the template behind it?
questions.follow_up: Who read the rewrite before it went out?

questions.question_text: Tell me about moving work forward with people who did not report to you and held different priorities. What did you try before escalating?
questions.follow_up: What did you learn about what those people were measured on?

questions.question_text: A team you depend on will not commit to a date, and you cannot travel to them or sit in their planning sessions. How do you get the dependency moving?
questions.follow_up: When would you decide to stop waiting, and who would you tell?

questions.question_text: Describe a disagreement with another team that you lost. How did you behave in the month afterwards?
questions.follow_up: Did you revisit it later, and on what basis?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a time you changed a piece of work because of something a customer said. What exactly did they say?
questions.follow_up: How did you check that they spoke for more than themselves?

questions.question_text: You are building for people whose circumstances are unlike yours: carers, people with very little time, people supporting children of their own. How do you find out what they actually need?
questions.follow_up: How would you know if you had got it wrong?

questions.question_text: Describe the last time you watched somebody use something you built. What surprised you?
questions.follow_up: What did you do about it that week?

questions.question_text: Tell me about something you carried past the interesting part, to the point where someone else could rely on it unattended.
questions.follow_up: What was the last unglamorous thing you had to do to get it there?

questions.question_text: Describe something you took from a prototype to a service other people depend on. How did you decide it had graduated out of your own care and into the team's?
questions.follow_up: What did you hand over with it?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a commitment you missed. Who found out first, and how did they find out?
questions.follow_up: What changed in the way you commit now?

questions.question_text: Bring me a table or a chart you relied on. What did it not say, and how did you state that limit to the people reading it?
questions.follow_up: Did they read it the same way you did?

questions.question_text: A number you publish every week moves sharply and nobody changed anything. What do you check, and in what order?
questions.follow_up: At what point do you tell the readers rather than keep looking?

questions.question_text: Describe a time you were asked for a measure that could not honestly be produced. What did you give instead?
questions.follow_up: How did that land with the person who asked?

questions.question_text: Tell me about feedback that was hard to give. What did you say about the behavior and about its effect?
questions.follow_up: What did you do differently the following week?

questions.question_text: Describe feedback you took badly at the time. What did you do with it once you had cooled off?
questions.follow_up: Would the person who gave it say you took it well in the end?

questions.question_text: Somebody you mentor keeps solving the wrong problem well. How do you handle the next session with them?
questions.follow_up: How would you know it had worked?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a quarter with more demand than capacity. What did you say would not be done, and who did you say it to?
questions.follow_up: How did you revisit that once the constraint moved?

questions.question_text: Two teams need the same week of your time and both have a reason. What do you do before you choose?
questions.follow_up: What do you write down once you have chosen?

questions.question_text: Describe something you cut that you wanted to keep. What made the cut defensible six months later?
questions.follow_up: Did anybody ask for it back?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a piece of work you connected to an account, a renewal or a pipeline. What would have made that connection false?
questions.follow_up: Did anybody test it, or was it taken on trust?

questions.question_text: You are asked to build something that only one customer will ever use. How do you decide, and what do you ask for first?
questions.follow_up: What would you need to see to change your mind?

questions.question_text: Describe a time the commercial argument for your own work was weaker than you had assumed. What did you do once you knew?
questions.follow_up: Who did you tell first, and why that person?

questions.question_text: Tell me about a process that survived your absence. What made it survive?
questions.follow_up: What broke the first time you were out of reach?

questions.question_text: You inherit a process with no records and no handover. What do you build first?
questions.follow_up: How do you know when it is enough?

questions.question_text: Describe the checks you put around a piece of work so that a stranger could run it. What did you deliberately leave manual?
questions.follow_up: What did that decision cost you?
